page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 model running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a massive local storage capacity of 120,000 GB of NVMe SSDs. Network connectivity is supported by a 300 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, scoring 287,164.37 on stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and 20,677.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Memory performance is exceptionally strong, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 13,947.51 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 258.51 GB/sec. Database operations are highly optimized, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 46,115.93 and a Redis SET throughput of 378.59 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,666.0, and LLM text generation is poor, yielding only 28.16 tokens per second on a small 135M model.

The hardware profile offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with high-capacity DDR5 memory and a high core count. This makes the server highly cost-efficient for large-scale data-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The primary tradeoffs include the lack of a dedicated GPU and the lower single-threaded performance inherent to the 2.7 GHz ARM architecture. This server is best suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
